tool_schemas.description: Current version per region, health and error rate of a service.

tool_schemas.name: list_deployments
tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: deploy
tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: create_incident
tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying checkout-api v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service failed health checks with an error rate of ~18%. Rolled back all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. (v2.3.1-rc was healthy only in staging, so it was not used.) After the rollback, all three regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is ~0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression before redeploying.

trace.final:
checkout-api is healthy again. I rolled it back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001.

- **Problem:** The latest release, v2.3.1, was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks with an error rate of about 18%.
- **Rollback:** I rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. I didn't use v2.3.1-rc because it was only ever healthy in staging. The rollback was to an earlier production release, not a new deploy, so it didn't need change-manager approval.
- **Result:** All three regions are now on v2.3.0. The service passes health checks and the error rate is down to about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 is open and has paged the on-call engineer. It says what failed, what I rolled back to and why, and how the service looks now. It also includes a follow-up: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying it.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0 (v2.3.1-rc was only healthy in staging).
